current_answer: People have built games, browser demos, desktop apps, art, brain engines and research tests on real fruit fly connectomes, mainly FlyWire (female brain) and MaleCNS (male brain and nerve cord). We checked 107 of them on 3 October 2026: 37 can be opened in a browser or free notebook without installing anything. Does it actually run? In our own check of six fly-brain browser demos in headless Chromium 154 on a Linux server without a GPU (3 Oct 2026, not a play test), 3 ran: Fly Worker (17.55 MB downloaded), FLY67 (33.28 MB) and flybrain.app (12.72 MB). FlyLeno and Help the Fly Escape loaded and then froze, most likely because our machine draws 3-D graphics in software, and fly-brain (Lulzx) stopped at our 1.6 GB memory limit. No demo computed its brain on a server; where we could locate it, the brain ran in a Web Worker in the browser tab (flybrain.app also tries a chat WebSocket, so for it the location is unclear). Safari, Firefox, phones and GPU machines were not tested. Most viral demos really run a simulated fly brain, but a person chose which neurons receive the input and which neurons act, and several get most of their movement from scripts or trained parts; no fly has been "uploaded". "I Taught a Fly How to Play Gorilla Tag (seriously)" (724,625 views on 3 Oct 2026) still names no model, data or code and stays U; all 20 verdicts were re-checked on 3 Oct (13 with code unchanged since graded, 7 with no code). Does the real fly wiring help? Sometimes: fly wiring beat scrambled wiring in 11 of 26 studies, mostly reflex, sensory and steering circuits; in trained, reservoir, ML, game and our walking tests it tied or lost (8). A chess-learning FlyWire mushroom body rates 1680 Elo with real wiring, 1675 shuffled and 1850 with a random design. fly-cartpole's redesigned flight circuit now beats its shuffled wiring (499.9 vs 165.9 steps), but its own linear map (499.6) and LQR (500) do as well, so the no-brain baseline is not beaten. Across 15 studies with a no-brain baseline the fly network beats it in only 2; in Doom a brainless autopilot survives 51.93 s against the fly brain's 53.34 s (doom-fly-control by gabrycina). In our own walking test, a scrambled brain and no brain walked the FlyGym fly as far as the real brain. flyvis, the connectome-constrained fly vision model, predicts the ON/OFF preference of all 32 characterised cell types (ensemble median) but has never been compared with a shuffled-wiring network. A beginner can run the published whole-brain model on a CPU: in our test on 2 CPUs (Linux, 28 minutes) sugar input drove MN9 to 85.2 Hz and shuffled wiring dropped it to 0 Hz; on 2 Oct 2026 we also tested connecting it to a FlyGym body.

catalogue_card.question: What have people built with the digital fruit fly brain, and what is real?
catalogue_card.text: 107 fruit fly brain simulation projects checked in code: 37 you can try online (6 loaded in our own browser check, 3 ran), 52 demo and lab videos with evidence grades, verdicts on 20 viral claims with check dates, 34 control studies, and our own tests.

summary: 107 entries checked on 3 Oct 2026 (3 new in the seventh check): 23 grade A, 21 B, 26 C, 4 D, 9 U and 24 datasets or tools (not graded).

Does it actually run? (made by us, procedure written down at 09:38:51 UTC on 3 Oct 2026 before the first load): six browser demos in headless Chromium 154, Linux, 2 CPUs, no GPU, one README action each, 60-90 s. Ran: Fly Worker 17.55 MB (7.55 MB brain file in a Web Worker), FLY67 33.28 MB (two connectome parts in a Web Worker; our earlier 'about 100 MB' estimate corrected), flybrain.app 12.72 MB (also tries a chat WebSocket, so where its brain runs is unclear). Loaded, then froze in our no-GPU browser: FlyLeno 33.95 MB (31.36 MB connectome reached a Web Worker), Help the Fly Escape 2.57 MB (its 9.9 MB brain graph never arrived). Stopped at our 1.6 GB memory limit: fly-brain (Lulzx) 33.93 MB, on both loads. No demo computed on a server. webgpu-fly (20 s extra record) did not start without a GPU adapter. Not a play test; Safari, Firefox, phones and GPU machines untested.

flyvis (Lappalainen et al. 2024): 45,669 neurons, 64 cell types, 721 columns, 734 trained parameters; ensemble median right on ON/OFF preference for 32 of 32 cell types (best model 30 of 32); r = 0.60, P = 2.6e-6 between task performance and direction-selectivity prediction; 26 studies; all quoted from the full text. Correction: direction selectivity can be predicted without synapse counts; only the T4/T5 preferred direction needs single-neuron detail. The authors' 50 pretrained models: validation loss median 5.300, range 5.137-5.678 (training task, not biology). Code and pretrained models MIT; connectome FlyEM FIB-25/FIB-19, no separate data licence stated. No shuffled-wiring control (a referee asked for one).

Controls ledger (3 Oct 2026): 34 studies, 26 with a wiring null: helps 11, no difference 6, worse 2, mixed 6, not yet scored 1. New: ChessFly (no difference, partly fair, weak: one fly and one shuffle per arm). fly-cartpole re-read at a8c6257 moved from no difference to helps (499.9 vs 165.9 steps, p = 0.0001) but does not beat its own linear map (499.6) or LQR (500). No scoring rule changed. Our walking test (2 Oct): real brain 13.93 mm, scrambled 14.15 mm, brainless constant drive 14.28 mm in 1 s; our mapping caps the drive.

Our 1 Oct fair test on the sugar reflex: real wiring 85.2 ± 3.56 Hz; degree-preserving and weight shuffles 0 Hz (5 each); boundary-preserving 39 ± 1.22 Hz (retention 0.46); sign shuffle 214 ± 43 Hz with the whole brain ignited (activity runaway, 258 times real). Gain check finished on 2 Oct: x2.5 matched shuffle 3 but not shuffles 4 and 5, so not matched on 3 shuffles; MN9 stayed at 0 Hz at every gain (0.37 to 2.12 times the real activity). The row stays mixed, unfair and weak.

Where the wiring helps, a brain-free baseline often matches the fly anyway: the fly network beats a no-brain baseline in only 2 of 15 studies. In Doom (doom-fly-control by gabrycina, commit 6b22922) the fly survives 53.34 s, shuffled wiring 6.75 s, a brainless autopilot 51.93 s and the best of 12 autopilot settings 53.44 s.

"I put a fly's brain into Terraria. And tried to train it" (George Ostrobrod, 0nniju8lLxk; 32,632 views on 3 Oct 2026): grade B from the GitLab code at 9052966d (older than the video). A checksummed MaleCNS v1.0 connectome with reward-modulated plasticity drives a Terraria body through hand-mapped sensory and motor populations; we recomputed its 176-life log (median 102.8 s first 44 lives vs 163.3 s last 44, p = 0.037); no plasticity-off or scrambled-wiring control.

"I Taught a Fly How to Play Gorilla Tag (seriously)" (724,625 views on 3 Oct 2026) and a Roblox fight video (144,054): both grade U, no code. Pokémon on a Raspberry Pi and the Rainbow Six Siege claim: still U. A driving compilation (63,935 views in 14 hours) appears to show Flyhard (B), matched from its thumbnail only. Every verdict row now shows its last check: 13 code unchanged since graded, 7 no code, 0 changed.

New entries (3 Oct 2026): ChessFly (A, a negative result: real FlyWire mushroom-body wiring 1680 Elo vs shuffled 1675 vs random design 1850 after 10,000 self-play games), flypoker (C: the hand equity is computed outside the brain) and neurafly (C: an audio visualiser that reads the neurons it injects into).

The choice of null changes answers: in flyconnectome-nulls standard nulls beat the connectome (1.78 and 1.77 vs 1.57) but boundary-keeping nulls tie it (1.58 and 1.62); in our own reflex test four nulls give silent, partly and runaway; in our walking test the readout (our capped mapping) left the wiring little room to matter.

37 entries have a no-install link; all answered our HTTP check on 3 Oct 2026, and 6 browser demos were also loaded in our headless browser (3 ran). FlyDoom (eganeganegan) returned HTTP 404 on 1, 2 and 3 Oct 2026; its link status is now 'gone' and its record is kept.

In viral demos a real connectome usually runs, but people chose the input and output neurons; DesktopFly, FlyCraft, Bad Apple, FlyDrones, the FlyBridge Minecraft farming demo and the Roblox maze race get much of their visible behaviour from scripts, stimulus, training or a synthetic network, and the Half-Life demo (grade D) builds a synthetic network by default.
Video gallery (3 Oct 2026): 52 videos, 46 of them original uploads, all available; 34 of 107 catalogue entries have at least one video. Thumbnails unchanged.
"91%" is the share of 164 testable predictions of the brain-only Shiu et al. 2024 model that matched experiments; "95%" compares versions of the model and is not an accuracy.
FlyWire data is CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial); MaleCNS, MANC, hemibrain and BANC data are CC BY.

Build your own: tested 28 Sep 2026 and re-tested 1 Oct 2026 on Linux with 2 CPUs (MN9 85.2 Hz real, 0 Hz shuffled; 82.0 Hz bit-exact). The deeper path Add a body is tested since 2 Oct 2026: brain tested (Python 3.11), body tested (uv, CPython 3.12.11, flygym 2.1.0, MUJOCO_GL=disable; set TMPDIR to a folder with about 400 MB free), mapping ours; FlyGym 2.0 rewrote the interface, so 1.x code does not run unchanged.
uncertainty: Our body test covers one stimulus (P9 at 150 Hz on both sides), one brain model, one body, 1 s of open-loop walking, 3 trial seeds and 3 shuffles that sent identical drives. The rate-to-drive mapping is ours: it caps the drive at 1.2, so another mapping could let the wiring matter more. The pre-registered P9 sign, other P9 rates and other descending neuron types were not tested in the body.

Our fair test covers one reflex (sugar to MN9) in one model, with one 1 s trial per shuffle at one trial seed; the MN9 rate cannot tell selective drive from global ignition. The gain-matched arm is not matched on 3 shuffles; a per-shuffle gain search has not been run.

Browser check: one headless Chromium 154 on Linux without a GPU, 60-90 s per demo, one action each; not a play test. Both freezes most likely come from software WebGL on our machine; GPU machines, Safari, Firefox and phones were not tested. Activity detection is coarse (screenshots every 5 s), bytes cover only the first 60-90 s, and traffic in cross-origin frames is not counted. Protocol completions and three deviations (a tool bug fixed and re-run within the 2-load limit) were written down but not pre-registered by the planner. View counts come from YouTube search pages; the Terraria, Gorilla Tag and Roblox fight videos were not watched.
The Terraria verdict rests on code older than the video; fly-walking-wiring's B is provisional because its results are not public. The Flyhard match of the driving compilation rests on one thumbnail.

Controls ledger: every number except our own two tests is the authors'. We recomputed 14 studies from their committed files but re-ran none; none is replicated, and only 2 of 34 are peer-reviewed. Only 10 of 34 studies reach "strong" method quality; 19 are weak. fly-cartpole's new numbers were not recomputed and its real arm sits at the 500-step ceiling; ChessFly rests on one fly and one shuffle per arm.

Ledger labels (wiring effect, fairness, quality) come from fixed yes/no rules applied to code and files; they are consistent but coarse. Our body test scores strong although its 3 shuffles behaved as one; our reflex test is "mixed" by rule although its arms read silent, partly and runaway. We did not override the rules for our own rows. Activity fields are reported only for our two tests. Retention puts very different measurements on one scale. The flyvis ablation values exist only in a figure and were not extracted; our text search of its supplement was crude (no PDF tool).

The "helps" results are mostly one kind of test (does a reflex pathway still carry signal after rewiring?), which is a low bar; boundary-preserving nulls have been applied to one reflex (ours: 46% kept), not to the other reflex studies.

Borderline grades: FlyLeno (B, borderline C); Fly Worker, fly-brain by Lulzx, The Fly's Hash Function, Fly OCR, Fly Self Driving, the null-model study and fly-brain-zero-shot are borderline A; fly-brain by erojas and Kick the Fly could argue B; acamilo-flybrain would sit on the B/C border without its stream macros.

Several C grades and the fafbseg entry rest on file citations that we spot-read but did not re-verify line by line. fly-plays-games runs its neurons in an external package (fly.ai) that we did not inspect beyond its commit subjects.

The Pokémon stream and the Rainbow Six claim are known only through news articles, a Reddit post and a Twitch page read through summarising tools or search summaries; X, TikTok and Reddit cannot be searched without a login.
Stars, creation and last-push dates of some records were reused from earlier checks and are labelled with those dates in projects.json.

Not yet triaged: about 30 new low-star repositories from this week, leads deferred in earlier weeks, about 211 repositories listed only in directories, and a widely seen Minecraft fly video (571,248 views) not yet mapped to a project.

Why the Shiu v783 file has 616 fewer neurons than the FlyWire v783 release is not established; the scope of BANC's "approximately 188,000 neurons" is not stated. The attractor reported for the Shiu et al. model has not been reproduced by us.

The Build your own guide is untested on macOS, Windows/WSL, Colab and machines with a C++ compiler; GitHub Pages publishing is untested. Add a body is tested on Linux CPU only, without rendering. DOOMFLY's and DesktopFly's run steps are untested by us.
FlyWire data licence conflict: CC BY-NC 4.0 in the official guidelines vs CC BY 4.0 on the Zenodo v783 record; we follow the stricter, non-commercial reading.
Video summaries rest on titles, descriptions, captions, code and thumbnails; we did not watch every video frame by frame. View counts are snapshots.

Videos cannot play inside the site: YouTube, Vimeo, TikTok and X players failed in the site's sandboxed frames (tested in headless Chromium only). YouTube and X thumbnails are loaded from their image servers.
freshness_note: Catalogue re-checked 3 Oct 2026 (107 entries, 3 new); six browser demos loaded in our headless browser 3 Oct 2026; all 20 verdicts re-checked 3 Oct 2026; video gallery re-checked 3 Oct 2026 (52 videos); controls ledger updated 3 Oct 2026 (34 studies).
